verdict.tagline: Complex engineering sandbox with a brutal start and deep building.
for_you_if: you enjoy intricate engineering and vehicle design
you can push past a steep initial learning curve
you want access to a massive community workshop
not_for_you_if: you need a functional tutorial right away
you expect steady frame rates on massive builds
you plan to play on the Steam Deck

citations.review_text:
Terrible game. Not like advertised. You want to fly a plane -- press thousands buttons and maybe you can drive a bit and crash into a mountain. You want to drive a ship -- Have fun..it will bounce on the water and then suddenly the front goes up and sinks it.

Rating: 1/10 (Only because I can’t give it a zero)

Playtime: Too too too too many hours spent hoping it would get better.

I don't think I have ever felt a sense of absolute disappointment quite like the one I feel after playing Stormworks. I bought this game with so much excitement, completely sold on a dream, and it has left me with nothing but massive regret and genuine sadness over how utterly broken and exhausting it actually is.

The Macabui Trap
Let’s talk about the elephant in the room: Macabui. I watched the content, heard the praise, and fully bought into the hype. Macabui made this game look like an intricate, rewarding, and highly polished engineering playground where your creativity could truly thrive. Nothing—and I mean nothing—lived up to what Macabui said.

What was promised to be a deep, satisfying simulation is actually just a chaotic, buggy chore. The video showcases and glowing reviews gave me a vision of a functioning game, but the reality is an unoptimized, frustrating mess that completely respects neither your time nor your effort.

Why It Is a Miserable Experience
The Physics are Farcical: For a game that relies entirely on physics, the engine is completely cooked. Boats behave like bouncy castles on trampoline water, aerodynamics feel like they were coded by someone who has never seen an airplane, and multi-grids are a literal ticking time bomb.

The Content is Devoid of Life: Once you get past the novelty of building something, you realize the actual "game" part is completely hollow. The missions are repetitive, the world feels dead and empty, and the AI is profoundly stupid.

A Continuous Cycle of Bugs: Every single update seems to break more things than it fixes. You will spend hours meticulously wiring logic panels and balancing fuel-to-air ratios, only for a minor patch to completely break your vehicle's mechanics out of nowhere.

Final Thoughts
It breaks my heart because the concept of this game is everything I wanted. But instead of …

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the controls as unresponsive, slippery, and hard to learn, and state that the build user interface is frustrating to fight against.

citations.review_text: I want to like this game, but the developer is putting the cart before the horse here. The main menu has a request feature option, but the existing mechanics need a lot of work. Slippery movement, unresponsive controls, and the fact that it is possible to softlock the tutorial spoils the potential this concept has. I would not touch any of the DLC and I think this game needs more time to bake. This is like the curse of so many EA developers (this game isn't even early access), always moving on to new content without finishing the job on what is already there. Have some confidence in your idea as is, do numerous passes ad nauseum until the game as is meets the vision you have for its quality, and then entertain new features. Had to refund after trying to enjoy the game only to be blocked by lacking fundamentals. I was excited when I saw the trailer, but sadly let down by the experience.

cohorts.summary: Experienced builders utilize community creations while navigating intricate physics systems.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the building and physics mechanics as having a steep learning curve with minimal in-game tutorials.

citations.review_text:
This game is impressive, complicated, and will probably make you question your life choices at least once.

You can play it in Story/Survival mode, or jump into kind of "Creative" mode and start building whatever your imagination comes up with. And when I say "building," I mean spending 45 minutes constructing a machine that looks like it should work, only to discover that you forgot one tiny component and now the whole thing is basically an expensive metal coffin.

The building and physics mechanics have a pretty steep learning curve. It takes a while to understand how everything works, but honestly, that's half the fun. Figuring out how to build something that actually works is just as satisfying as figuring out how to operate the damn thing without immediately turning yourself into a meteorite.

Not interested in spending hours trying to become an engineer through trial and error? No problem. The Workshop has an absolutely ridiculous number of creations to try. Some of them are so complicated that I'm pretty sure the creator has a degree in Mechanical Engineering and possibly a direct line to NASA. Others are basically "press WASD and click something." There's something for everyone.

The graphics are... fine. Let's put it that way. You can't really expect cutting-edge visuals from a game that's already making your PC work overtime just to calculate whether your homemade monstrosity should physically remain in one piece. The relatively simple graphics probably help the game run on less powerful machines, which is definitely a good thing.

That said, if you want to really push the game and take full advantage of the building and simulation systems, you're going to want a decent PC. I'd recommend at least an 11th-gen CPU and an RTX 3060. Your GPU won't necessarily be the one crying first, though. The physics simulation might decide that your CPU has had it too easy.

The sound design is pretty good too. Engines sound like engines, wind sounds like wind, steam whist…
excellent game could use a tutorial that explains more but nonethless its a great game the engine requirements are simple to understand if yoy have wikipedia
Good building game with in depth systems. Since there is almost no tutorial it is required to invest hours reading / watching guides and videos, but it's worth it.

Once you take time to learn the mechanics of the game it becomes highly addicting. The Search and Destory addon Is mandatory because it adds a way to make the game more enjoyable with friends. Overall 8.9 out of 10 because of the learning curve and can crash when typing in the chat.

cohorts.summary: Longtime players face performance slowdowns and frame drops during large engineering projects.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the physics engine runs on a single core or thread, contributing to performance slowdowns and game speed dropping during large builds.

citations.review_text:
Best concept, worst implementation. It feels almost like you've been tasked to make a salad and given best ingredients. And yet, you just shoved them into the blender and then sell this smoothie as if it deserves the price... 

At first this game was for me a great alternative to Scrap Mechanic that offered more complex systems and engines, somewhat better physics and overall more possibilities for different vehilces. But the more I kept playing, the more I realized how much flaws it has. Physics running on single core, bad multiplayer with frequent ghost chunks (that freeze you on client side), sudden crashes and the list goes on... And for all this you have to pay just 2k ₽ (for Russia), for US it's 55$ in total. Can't say I'm stingy or something, it just not worth it (opposite example - Scrap Mechanic)...

Can argue endlessly about StormDon'tWorks: Dismay & Disaster and how the potential is ruined, so I'll be brief. If you wanna experience the first excitement being replaced by the disappointment - go on. Otherwise, better save your money for something else.

P.S. Message for Geometa Studios. Not sure you'll be even reading it, but if you decided to abandon the game, why not make it open-source, or maybe just make an open SDK like Valve did with TF2? (No matter how cynical this might sound) The fans will do all the work when you'll continue making money. Sounds like a business plan, doesn't it?..

THE DEVS DON'T CARE ABOUT THE OPTIMALIZATION!!

I have almost 300 hours in this game. I haven't played survival or missions, all I did was building ships and trains. The variety of the components is fine, you can build a lot of cool creations, even if you know how to edit XML files.

But the physics lately made this game unplayable. The physics engine runs on a single thread, which makes the game incredibly slow, even on low settings. Not laggy, slow. The game literally forces you into slow motion instead of lagging, to make you feel even more miserable. The devs don't care about the community or the game, they only care about the cash that comes from sales. The DLCs are overpriced and doesn't worth it, only for the couple of building blocks and features that are important.

I want to love the game as much as I want, but I just can't. The base idea is really good, and if the game was opitimized I would play it 24/7 I think. But in this state I physically can't.

6/10

I wanted to get into the game, but the lag is unbearable and I can't play it anymore. 
The physics engine apparently runs off of a single thread, which leaves the game in constant slow motion. With AI ships disabled, no player ships spawned, and with settings set to low the most the game can run at is 2/3 it's full speed. It just never stops lagging.
The final straw for me trying to run around the artic with no vehicles spawned anywhere and the physics engine managing to reach as low as 10fps which is very slow.
I know it's not my setup either. I have a Ryzen 7 3700x which isn't the latest sure but it's almost as old as this game is. It was the best processor for gaming at the time when this game release. I doubt having the latest CPU is going to be enough to take the game from 10 to 60fps anyways.
The game just doesn't work properly and I can't recommend anyone waste their money on something that won't work.

claims.claim: Reviewers mention that large vehicles or complex creations cause frame drops, freezing, or performance issues on lower-end computers.

citations.review_text: Worth the $25 dollar price tag, although I would point out if one were to design a large vehicle or use mods to expect some frame drops and performance issues (if using a low end or office computer), but other than that I have no complaints on this game it is highly recommended for those who are interested in vehicle creation, aviation, or naval design with an easy to understand interface and realistic physics engine. 10/10 would pay full price for this game.

This is a great game, especially with the search and destroy DLC. The workshop has lots of fun vehicles and practically infinite content. 

However:
This game is NOT well optimised, especially when playing multiplayer. I know my pc isnt the latest build with some 5090 or something but come on devs. Most of the time its ok but this game sometimes just randomly dies which leaves you flying a helicopter at 1 tick per 3 seconds.

Its a good game despite these issues (which is why i have 133hours at time of writing) and its lots of fun to play with friends but this game needs a LOT of optimisation to be a good, enjoyable, playable game.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game has a very steep learning curve with a lack of in-game guidance for learning core systems and mechanics.

citations.review_text: One of the best games I have played in a while. The learning curve is steep if you want to build nice looking builds, but it has thousands of hours of playtime! I would say that it is worth it to buy, but only if you are ready for many hours of learning.

Do you have ADHD? Do you have a touch of the tism? Well, this is the game for you.

As of writing this review, I'm at 371 hours (15.45 days) played. Some people might think I know what I'm doing in this game. Those people would be wrong.

This is, by far, the best sandbox game I've ever played.

Pros:
-No limit to your imagination.
-Design and build whatever you want.
-Missions to test your creations.
-MULTIPLAYER SANDBOX!!!
-Huge modding/community workshop scene. You can easily lose hours just scrolling through creations.

Cons:
-Graphics are okay, but the terrain could be smoother.
-Not very well optimized. It freezes occasionally.
-Land AI doesn't do much.
-Very steep learning curve. There's a lot to learn, but not a lot of guidance.
-You can't build simultaneously with friends. Understandable, but it would be really cool.

Overall:
Clearly, with 371 hours played, I love this game, and several of my friends do too. The sequel is supposed to come out this year, and from what I've seen in the trailers, it looks like it addresses many of the issues listed above.

10/10. Would buy again. Worth every hour and every dollar.

After owning this game for 3 years, its amazing. Stormworks has its flaws with building like not being able to get certain shapes without xml editing (trust me, its not as complicated as it sounds), but aside from that its perfect if you love to make something of your own and enjoy alot of engineering. It has a very steep learning curve and its definitely intimidating to most but it gets your brain going, once you even vaguely understand the mechanics, you can make something amazing but it definitely takes time. With that said, its not for everyone and you never stop learning but if you want to make big builds like even 0.5/0.6 : 1, your going to need a fairly decent computer to run it, my only wish is the game could handle things like aircraft carriers but eventually you will learn your way around and find what works for you.

All in all, its a great game and it doesnt even feel like ive spent 1100 hours in it and the developers actually listen to the playerbase and add what we want (aslong as it actually fits and works in the game, obviously). I would 1000% recommend and if you get stuck on something, theres millions of tutorials on youtube to help you out!
